bugs.summary: 'reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype' fails to reconcile slot classes inherited from multiple superclasses

comments.text:
Here, `reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype` (called from `setClass`) tests `extends("logical", "vector")` and so does not complain:

```
> setClass("A", contains = "VIRTUAL", slots = c(x = "logical"))
> setClass("B", contains = "VIRTUAL", slots = c(x = "vector"))
> setClass("AB", contains = c("A", "B"))
> showClass("AB")
Class "AB" [in ".GlobalEnv"]

Slots:
              
Name:        x
Class: logical

Extends: "A", "B"
```

Here, it tests `extends("vector", "logical")` and fails unnecessarily:

```
> setClass("BA", contains = c("B", "A"))
Error in reconcilePropertiesAndPrototype(name, slots, prototype, superClasses,  : 
  Definition of slot 'x', in class "BA", as "vector" conflicts with definition, inherited from class "A", as "logical"
```

Surely in both cases it should rather check each of `extends("logical", "vector")` and `extends("vector", "logical")`, keeping the more specific class (in this case `"logical"`) if either is `TRUE` and failing if both are `FALSE`?  Then the behaviour would be robust to the order of superclasses in `contains`.

A work-around is to specify directly the reconciled slot class:

```
> setClass("BA", contains = c("B", "A"), slots = c(x = "logical"))
> showClass("BA")
Class "BA" [in ".GlobalEnv"]

Slots:
              
Name:        x
Class: logical

Extends: "B", "A"
```

But then one loses one of the conveniences of the inheritance mechanism.  I'm exploring a patch ...
